patients.summary: Healthy young business development associate who joined in 2022. Two ED presentations a year apart, in 2025 and 2026, for hypomanic episodes brought in by her sister, each leading to an inpatient psychiatric stay; after the second she carries bipolar II disorder on quetiapine, followed by outpatient psychiatry. Records arrive late or not at all.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new PCP, says her old office stopped taking new appts for routine physicals and she wants somewhere she can actually reach a doctor. 25 y/o, BCBS PPO, verified. No current meds per pt. Booked new pt physical 9/14 at 8:40. Release form for prior office sent through portal; pt will sign tonight.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wendy is a 25-year-old woman establishing care. Wants a physical and a doctor she can text. Works in business development for a software firm, a lot of calls and some travel. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother has bipolar I disorder. Paternal grandfather had major depression. No known heart disease, diabetes or cancer in parents.
Social: single, lives in town. Has never smoked. Does not drink at all. No drug use. Walks and does a spin class twice a week.
Gyn: regular cycles. Last Pap 2021 at her old office, normal per pt; records requested.
Immunizations: HPV series as a teen, Tdap 2019 per her old office.

ROS: negative across systems. Sleep 7 hrs. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant, organized. Vitals in flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rashes or concerning lesions. Neuro grossly intact. Calm, euthymic, linear thought.

Assessment and plan:
1. Health maintenance, 25F. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids and TSH drawn. One-time HIV and hep C screens drawn, she agrees. Flu vaccine today, right deltoid. Pap not due until 2024.
2. Family history of bipolar disorder in her mother: noted. She has no history of mood episodes herself.
Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Eleven pages from her previous primary care office. Includes: annual visit notes 2019 to 2021 (no problems listed, no meds), Tdap 6/2019, Pap 8/2021 NILM, adolescent immunization record with three HPV doses in 2009. Abstracted to immunizations and screening. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, everything from your physical came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you last week.

documents.title: Vaccine administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for bivalent COVID booster. Last dose over a year ago per her card. Denies fever or illness today. 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. Observed 15 minutes, felt fine and left. Card updated.

documents.title: Form for work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my company does a wellness incentive and they need a provider to sign that I had a physical in the last 12 months. I uploaded the form. Is that something you can fill out?

documents.title: RE: Form for work
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Wendy, the doctor signed it this morning. It is attached here as a PDF so you can submit it yourself.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26F, annual. Busy year at work, says she is fine. Sleeping okay, exercising when she can. No new symptoms. Still no meds, no tobacco, no alcohol.

PHQ-2 0.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. Well, cheerful. Neck supple, no nodes. RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. No edema. Skin fine.

Plan: Doing well. Labs from last year all normal, nothing needed today. Flu and the 2023 COVID vaccine given, one in each arm. Pap due next fall. See her in a year.

documents.body: Could I get a copy of my vaccine history? HR is updating files.

documents.title: RE: Vaccine record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Attached your full immunization record, including the HPV doses and Tdap from your old office and everything given here.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, age 27. Due for Pap. Feels great. Work going well. Periods regular. No meds. Never smoker, no ETOH.

PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: BP and weight as charted, stable from last year. HEENT normal. RRR. CTAB. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, normal-appearing cervix, Pap collected, chaperone MA present. Skin clear. Mood good.

A/P: Healthy 27-year-old. Pap sent, cytology alone (next one 2027 if normal). Flu shot today; she will get the COVID booster at her pharmacy. No labs needed this year. Back next fall.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wendy, your Pap smear was normal. Next one in three years.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Visit of 03/12/2025, arrived 18:20.
Allergies: NKDA.

CC: brought in by sister for behavior change.

HPI: 28-year-old woman whose sister has noticed about ten days of change: she talks without stopping, has hardly slept, has been spending large amounts of money, and now says she is about to launch a company that will make her a billionaire. Patient reports roughly two hours of sleep a night for the past week and says she has never felt better.

PSH: third molar extraction age 18. Meds: none. Social: never smoker, no alcohol; works in business development. Family: mother with bipolar I; paternal grandfather with major depression.

Exam: Agitated, cannot sit still. Pressured, rapid speech; repeatedly talks over the examiner; attention drifts between topics. States she has unique insight into world finance. Not responding to internal stimuli. Physical exam otherwise without abnormality.

Results: screening labs unremarkable.

Impression: hypomanic episode.
Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry for safety and stabilization.

documents.title: Hospital stay
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted you to know I was in the hospital last week, the psych unit. My sister took me to the ER. I'm home now since Tuesday. They said to check in with my primary doctor. Can I get an appointment?

documents.title: RE: Hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Wendy, and I'm glad you're home. Our front desk will call you this morning with a time next week. If you feel unsafe or things start speeding up again before then, call me or go back to the ER.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after inpatient psychiatric stay at the regional hospital, 3/12 to 3/18. We have no records yet; history from Wendy.

She says her sister brought her to the ER after about a week and a half of barely sleeping and spending heavily on a business she was sure would take off. She was admitted. She remembers being told it was a hypomanic episode. Discharged Tuesday on no medication; she was told to find an outpatient psychiatrist. She has not called anyone yet. Sleeping about 8 hours now, back at work part days. Feels "a little embarrassed, mostly tired." No thoughts of harming herself. No alcohol or drugs.

PHQ-9 3.

Exam: Vitals fine. Calm, cooperative, normal rate of speech, linear. Mood "okay," affect appropriate. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P: Hypomanic episode, recent admission. Stable today. Records request faxed to the hospital for ED and discharge paperwork. Gave her the outpatient psychiatry intake line the hospital listed. Reviewed warning signs with her and her sister by speaker. Follow up in about 3 months.

documents.title: Records follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called hospital HIM re: discharge summary for March admission. ER record came 4/2, discharge summary not yet sent. Re-faxed request with signed release. Told it is in their queue.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt missed 6/18 follow-up. Left voicemail to rebook and sent portal reminder. No callback as of end of day.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization report
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State registry notice: influenza vaccine given 10/4/25 at a community pharmacy. Entered in immunization history.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wendy, 28, here for her physical. Last seen in March after her psychiatric admission; she missed the June recheck. Says she has felt like herself since spring. Working full time. Sleeping 7 to 8 hours. Has not set up with psychiatry; feels she does not need to. Flu shot already done at the pharmacy last month. Still no meds, never smoked, no alcohol.

PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: BP, pulse and weight in the flowsheet, all normal and steady. Pleasant, well groomed, normal speech, euthymic. Thyroid normal. RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Hypomanic episode in March, resolved. Marking resolved on the problem list. Hospital discharge summary still never arrived.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, TSH today. Pap current through 2027. Flu done.
Return in a year.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, your blood counts, chemistry panel and thyroid test are all normal.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 3/13/2026.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Chief concern: sister reports patient has not slept in three days and is acting unlike herself.

HPI: 29F with a hypomanic episode requiring admission here about a year ago presents with her sister for the same picture. Loud, fast speech; she is pulled off topic by noise in the hallway. Describes herself as able to do things others cannot. Has run up large online purchases, which her sister says is not like her. Patient denies any recent stressor, drug or alcohol use, or physical illness. Per sister, there have been two comparable spells in the last five years, each about a week long, each followed by a period of severe depression.

Meds: none. PSH: wisdom teeth age 18. FH: mother bipolar I, paternal grandfather MDD. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: VS within normal limits. No stigmata of drug use, not intoxicated. Mood euphoric, affect labile. Remainder of exam normal.

Data: CBC normal. Electrolytes normal. TSH and free T4 normal. Urine toxicology screen negative.

Impression: recurrent hypomanic episode. Psychiatry consulted; admit to inpatient psychiatric unit.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Inpatient Psychiatry Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient psychiatric unit.
Admitted 3/13/2026 from the ED. Discharged 3/20/2026.
Allergies: NKDA.

Reason for admission: second hypomanic presentation in roughly a year, three days without sleep, grandiosity and impulsive spending, brought by family.

Hospital course: Admitted voluntarily. Started on quetiapine at night and titrated to 100 mg at bedtime, tolerated with some morning sedation. Sleep normalized by day 4. Speech and goal-directed activity returned to baseline. Collateral from sister describes two prior elevated spells over five years with depressive stretches afterward. No suicidal ideation at any point. No substance use.

Discharge diagnosis: bipolar II disorder, most recent episode hypomanic.

Discharge medication: quetiapine 100 mg by mouth at bedtime.

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry intake 4/8/2026 (arranged). PCP follow-up within 1 to 2 weeks.

Condition at discharge: stable, future-oriented, denies SI/HI.

documents.title: External fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External Rx history flag: quetiapine 100 mg #30 filled 3/20/26, prescriber is a hospital psychiatrist. No hospital notification on file. Routed to RN to reach out.

documents.title: Outreach after new prescription
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt about new quetiapine fill. She confirms she was admitted to the psych unit 3/13 to 3/20 and went home on quetiapine nightly. Taking it. Groggy in the morning, otherwise okay. Denies SI. Sister staying with her this week. Scheduled with PCP Wed 3/25. Records request sent to hospital.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wendy comes in with her sister after her second psychiatric admission, 3/13 to 3/20. Hospital paperwork not received; we learned of the stay from the pharmacy fill. History from both of them.

About three days with no sleep, fast talking, big online purchases, feeling she could do anything. Same picture as last March. Her sister adds that there were two similar spells in the last five years, each about a week, each followed by weeks of deep depression; one was before Wendy joined us, and neither low stretch was ever brought to a doctor. The inpatient team told her the diagnosis is bipolar II disorder and started quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Psychiatry intake is set for 4/8.

Taking quetiapine every night. Sleeping 9 hours, slow to get going in the morning. Denies SI. No alcohol or drugs.

PHQ-9 5.

Exam: Vitals normal. Tired-appearing, calm, normal speech rate, linear and goal directed. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Bipolar II disorder, recent hypomanic episode with admission. Quetiapine 100 mg qhs per hospital; psychiatry to manage. Added to our list.
2. Medication counseling: discussed sedation, weight and metabolic effects; will check A1c and lipids in about two months. Talked about pregnancy planning and contraception while on psychiatric medication; she is not planning a pregnancy and will raise it with psychiatry before any change.
3. Records request re-sent to the hospital.
Follow up after the psychiatry intake, about 6 to 8 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Psychiatry intake letter (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry, community mental health group. Seen 4/8/2026.

Dear colleague,
Thank you for sharing the care of Ms. McGrath, 29, seen for intake after her March inpatient stay. She has bipolar II disorder with two documented hypomanic episodes needing admission (2025 and 2026) and, by family report, earlier elevated and depressive spells. Mother has bipolar I.

Since discharge she reports steady mood and good sleep on quetiapine 100 mg nightly. Morning fog is easing. No depressive symptoms now. No SI. No substances. Allergies: none known.

Mental status: well related, normal speech, euthymic, full affect, linear, no psychosis, good insight.

Plan: continue quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Psychotherapy referral within our group. Please obtain baseline metabolic labs (A1c, lipid panel) and weight; we will follow them with you. Return here in about three months.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Labs at your May visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, I got your psychiatrist's letter, and the hospital records finally came too. At your May 13 visit we'll draw the blood work they asked for (sugar and cholesterol). Nothing to fast for, but morning is easiest.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up for bipolar II on quetiapine 100 mg at night, now about 8 weeks in. Saw psychiatry 4/8, next visit there in July. Mood even. Sleeping 7 to 8 hours. Still a little groggy for the first hour of the day, manageable with coffee. Back at work full time. No racing thoughts, no spending sprees, no low mood. No SI. Taking it nightly.

PHQ-9 3.

O: Weight unchanged from March. BP and pulse normal. Bright, relaxed, normal speech. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no tremor.

A/P:
1. Bipolar II disorder, stable on quetiapine. Continue; psychiatry manages dosing.
2. Metabolic monitoring on an antipsychotic: A1c, lipid panel and CMP drawn today, weight recorded. Will send results to psychiatry.
3. Due for physical in the fall, flu then.
RTC fall.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: your A1c, cholesterol, liver and kidney tests are all in the normal range. I faxed a copy to your psychiatrist.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My pharmacy says my quetiapine needs a new prescription. Can you send it or does it have to be the psychiatrist?

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Wendy, since your psychiatrist manages that medication, please call their office for the refill. If they can't get to it before you run out, let us know and we'll bridge you.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Called them, they sent it. Thanks.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up letter (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry follow-up, 7/15/2026.

Ms. McGrath remains euthymic on quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. No hypomanic or depressive symptoms since discharge. Sleep regular. Mild morning sedation, tolerable. Metabolic labs from your office in May reviewed, normal. Engaged in therapy.

Plan: no change; continue quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Return in three months.

Outpatient psychiatry
